We want to move quickly and list our initial offering on AWS Marketplace as a private offer so we can capture the early-adopter cohort.

A few specifics from procurement:
- They want a revenue-share carveout for the first 12 months at 22% rev-share to support our go-to-market co-marketing.
- Net60 payment is standard for them, but they can consider Net45 if we provide an early-adopter credit.
- They will require our SOC2 report and a short data residency attestation.

Attached: BlueArc_EarlyAdopter_Rollup.xlsx (usage & forecast), Draft_PrivateOffer_Terms_v1.docx, Procurement_RFP_Response.pdf.

Can you escalate this to Deal Desk / Execs for exception review? The timing is tight — they want a signed private offer by end of May to qualify for the AWS promotional window.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer request — early adopter rev-share + payment term ask

Team — forwarding BlueArc's ask. TL;DR: they request 22% rev-share for 12 months and Net60 (willing to move to Net45 with credit). Commitment: 1-year private listing, initial forecast attached. AWS promotional timing is why they need speed.

My initial read: the rev-share baseline for Marketplace is usually 15% for this listing tier; 22% is above the typical threshold and will require exec exceptions. Procurement terms (Net45/60) and any up-front credit affect revenue recognition and billing cadence — finance needs to weigh in. Also need security proof (we can share SOC2) and a short attestation for data residency.

Asks:
1) Karthik / Deal Desk: can you model the unit economics if we approve 22% for 12 months vs 18%? Include impact on ARR revenue and margin over first 12 months. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/987654321/BA-202605EA-73
2) Marissa: this is a strategic early-adopter partner that could drive a category signal — would you recommend an exec exception?
3) Markus: Legal — quick read on the Draft_PrivateOffer_Terms_v1.docx and whether procurement requests (Net45 / credit) are acceptable.

I can coordinate a 30-min sync with BlueArc + exec sponsor if we get a green light. We should aim to have an approval decision by EOD Wed 20 May to meet their timeline.

--
Irene Choi
Director, GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer request — early adopter rev-share + payment term ask

Irene / team — I reviewed the forecast in BlueArc_EarlyAdopter_Rollup.xlsx and ran a quick sensitivity model. Key points below.

Summary of impact (12-month view):
- At 15% rev-share (standard) our net take is ~85% of listed gross ARR (after AWS fees & rev-share).
- At 22% rev-share, incremental margin pressure is material: ~6.5% revenue delta vs 15% which reduces our contribution margin on the listing by ~40% on year-one bookings for this account.
- If we structure a stepped rev-share (22% first 3 months, 18% next 9 months) we retain more upside while giving BlueArc marketing runway.

Payment terms: Net60 increases DSO and cashflow exposure. If we offer Net45 we should ask for either a 1% early-pay credit reversal or a $25k upfront onboarding credit to offset the cash timing.

Recommendations (deal desk):
1) Approve a conditional exception that allows a stepped rev-share: 22% for Q1 (90 days from listing) then 18% for the remainder of the 12 months. This is contingent on hitting the usage forecast in their rollup (tier triggers).
2) Approve Net45 but require a $25k non-refundable onboarding credit drawn against first invoices OR a 1% reduction to the rev-share if they pay within 15 days.
3) Security gating: require SOC2 attestation and a short data residency statement before listing goes live.

Next steps: If Marissa signs off, I'll escalate to finance for final cashflow signoff and to execs for approval (anything that changes effective rev-share >20% needs Exec signoff per policy). Markus — please confirm the contract redlines we need (payment / credit language + listing termination triggers).

Karthik
Senior Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Emma Johnson <emma@bluearclabs.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private offer request — early adopter rev-share + payment term ask

Emma — thanks for the materials and for moving fast. Internal team: after reviewing Karthik's modeling and the strategic upside, I'm approving an exception with the following final terms: 

Final terms (approved):
- Rev-share: Stepped structure — 22% for the first 90 days from listing, then 18% for the remaining 9 months.
- Payment terms: Net45. In exchange BlueArc accepts a $25,000 non-refundable onboarding credit that will be invoiced with the first invoice and applied against usage.
- Contract: Use the Draft_PrivateOffer_Terms_v1.docx as the base. Markus — please incorporate payment credit language, a 30-day termination for non-payment clause, and the AWS Marketplace listing removal trigger if usage falls 40% below forecast for 60 days.
- Security: Provide SOC2 report and sign a one-paragraph data residency attestation before we publish the private offer.

Conditions and runway: This exception is time-limited to this early-adopter program and will not set precedent; any renewal will be evaluated at standard Marketplace bands. Legal and finance will finalize redlines; once complete we will send the DocuSign envelope. Emma — please confirm you can accept the onboarding credit and provide SOC2 by end of week.

Emma, forwarding your original note below so legal has context. Once Markus confirms redlines, Karthik will coordinate the HubSpot deal update and finance will prepare the invoice schedule.

Best,
